RQ1.rationale: The paper develops a nanosatellite/CubeSat system model architecture and verification model, but it is an EIRSAT-1 communications-subsystem case rather than a general minimal-behavior reference model or EPS model.

RQ2.rationale: The paper claims MBSE-related traceability, automation, reuse, and effort/time savings, but not EPS-specific reliability/reproducibility/integrability outcomes and not with strong evidence.

RQ3.rationale: The paper integrates verification artifacts with a system/communications model and actual test setup, but it is not EPS-specific and not pre-physical-development verification.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Contrasts with INCOSE/OMG SSWG CubeSat MBSE articles that the authors say had not been applied to actual CubeSat missions; this paper is an EIRSAT-1 project-applied NSM pilot rather than a reusable SSWG reference model.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Implement the UCD Nanosatellite System Modeling project's MBSE approach across CubeSat lifecycle development and demonstrate requirements verification for EIRSAT-1 communications testing; motivation includes limited nanosatellite SE standards and need for traceable, automated verification.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: System model organized into packages for requirements, structure, use cases, behavior, analysis, EIRSAT-1 physical structure and V&V, ground segment, launch segment, launch/ground operations, and auxiliary value/signal types. The implemented exemplar focuses on TT&C and ground-segment communications rather than the whole spacecraft or EPS.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: The verification model is built from existing EIRSAT-1 requirements, design, test documents, and the traditional end-to-end communications test plan; it does not present a method for modeling with minimal behavioral knowledge.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.handling_limited_behavioral_knowledge: not reported; the case uses available project documents and test plans.
generality_reuse_mechanism: specific-mission model with reusable method only

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The EIRSAT-1 model is specific to one mission and the demonstrated exemplar is the communications subsystem, not a mission-agnostic architecture. Reuse is supported at the workflow/method level: OOSEM/SysML/CATIA Magic are used to construct verification models from test plans, interface them with scripts/hardware, and reuse/apply a similar approach in comparable verification scenarios and remaining subsystems. The interface-focused label is supported by the model-to-script/test-setup exchange and ground-segment interface modeling. Do not add high-level abstraction, mission-agnostic architecture, or low-dynamics / non-detailed-behavior model.

evidence.quote: As a starting point, we have adopted INCOSE OOSEM.

The aim is to construct the verification models in MBSE similar to the verification plans in traditional SE and create interface plugins to exchange information between the MBSE environment and the external test scripts.
The MBSE verification model allows the required technical parameters to flow from the system models to the Python client which in turn commands the ground station hardware
the models can be reused several times in similar verification scenarios
A similar approach will be applied to the remaining subsystems, creating a automated framework.

key_findings_by_rq.RQ1: Partial evidence for nanosatellite system-level MBSE architecture: EIRSAT-1 packages and OOSEM/SysML/CATIA Magic workflow are described, but not a general minimal-behavior or EPS reference model.
key_findings_by_rq.RQ2: Partial outcome evidence: claims include traceability, automated requirements verification, time/effort saving, reuse, and integration, but evidence is mostly qualitative single-case demonstration without quantitative baseline or EPS specificity.
key_findings_by_rq.RQ3: Partial verification relevance: verification procedures are integrated into system/communications models and actual test setup; not EPS-specific and not pre-physical-development verification.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: No single tool can fully meet all requirements for complete MBSE realization.
Only IBM Harmony and OOSEM were reviewed due to time constraints.
The reported work is a first step/preliminary NSM objective.
The actual implementation is focused on Phase C-D communications-subsystem testing and verification.
Broader lifecycle ecosystem integration and remaining subsystems are future work.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No EPS-specific model or verification evidence.
No pre-physical-development verification evidence; work uses actual end-to-end test setup after flight acceptance review.
No quantitative outcome metrics or measured baseline for claimed time/effort reduction.
No independent validation or repeated reuse across subsystems/projects.

open_researcher_observations: The paper is more valuable for MBSE-enabled V&V/toolchain continuity than for EPS modeling.
The system model appears to be retrofitted to a mature mission with existing documents rather than used from early design inception.
The strongest concrete mechanism is automated compliance-table updating from test outcomes; the strongest gap is lack of quantitative evaluation.
synthesis_consistency.lineage_consistency_notes: This should be compared with SSWG CubeSat MBSE/reference-model papers as a project-applied follow-on/contrast, but it is not itself a reusable reference model.
synthesis_consistency.extraction_confidence_reason: The paper is short and the relevant MBSE, context, and outcome claims are clear; confidence in extraction is high even though the paper's evidence for outcomes is limited.
